name: Pedaja
title: Son of King Jeconiah
summary: Pedaja was a son of King Jeconiah (Jehoiachin) of Judah, who was taken into captivity in Babylon. He is mentioned in the royal genealogies in 1 Chronicles and is an important link in the Davidic lineage leading to Jesus Christ. Through his son Zerubbabel (according to 1 Chronicles), his descendants played a central role in Israel's rebuilding after the exile.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in Jehoiachin's lineage
keyEvents.description: Pedahiah is listed as one of the sons of King Jehoiachin (Jeconiah), who was taken into exile in Babylon. This places him within the royal Davidic line.

keyEvents.title: Father of Zerubbabel
keyEvents.description: According to 1 Chronicles, Pedahiah was the father of Zerubbabel, who led the Jews back from Babylon and rebuilt the temple in Jerusalem.

keyEvents.title: Lineage to the Messiah
keyEvents.description: Pedahiah is a crucial link in the messianic lineage from King David through Jehoiachin down to Jesus Christ, as documented in the Gospel of Matthew.

keyEvents.title: Part of the royal exile line
keyEvents.description: As the son of the imprisoned King Jehoiachin, Pedahiah represented the Davidic monarchy in exile and kept alive the promise of a future Davidic king.

keyEvents.title: Zerubbabel's role in rebuilding the temple
keyEvents.description: Pedahiah's son Zerubbabel became the leader of the returning exiles and oversaw the reconstruction of the temple in Jerusalem, giving Pedahiah's family great significance in Israel's history.
